reviews.text:
Dear Cleanup Development Team,

I am writing to express my concerns regarding your Cleanup app and its pricing and privacy practices.

While the app is presented as a convenient solution for cleaning and optimizing iPhone storage, I am concerned about the cost of its subscriptions, particularly weekly pricing that can result in substantial annual expenses. I believe pricing should be presented clearly and transparently so that consumers can make informed decisions before committing to a subscription.

I am also concerned about the collection and potential use of personal data. Given that this application accesses sensitive information, including personal photos and videos, I expect a clear explanation of what information is collected, whether any data is transmitted to external servers, how that information is used, and whether it is shared with third parties for advertising or other purposes.

As a consumer, I believe the following practices are essential:

1. Transparent pricing: Clearly disclose all subscription fees and the total annual cost before users subscribe.
2. Honest marketing: Make the distinction between free and paid features immediately clear.
3. Privacy protection: Explain precisely what personal information is collected and whether photos and videos ever leave the user’s device.
4. Informed consent: Ensure users understand recurring billing terms before confirming a subscription.

reviews.title: App crashes every 30 seconds
reviews.text: With the app crashing every 30 seconds it’s nearly impossible to get anything done. It would only get one more star though. It’s not very smart - while reviewing similar videos it suggests a soccer game and last nights dinner - these are not similar. My biggest complaint is that it suggests to delete 20,000 similar images but you couldn’t possibly review that many at a time. They need to batch them into smaller groups. I’d like to see an option to select your group size. Reviewing 20 photos at a time, or 100, is much more reasonable. Once people trust the suggestions more they can delete 1000’s at a time maybe. I had to manually select each photo to delete because the only other option is to delete all 20,000 at once. I liked that it usually suggested to keep your favorited photo in a series of similar photos. I didn’t try the email or contacts features, just photos. It has a video compression option to lower the space used by videos. It also had a Live Photo to still photo conversion tool but again I couldn’t use them much because it wanted to convert 1000’s at a time rather than a small group I could review more easily. I’m deleting the app, since manually deleting one by one is exactly what I can do in the photo app on my phone and restarting every 30-60 seconds was making it absolutely worthless and frustrating.

reviews.title: AI is trash
reviews.text:
This program is based in AI apparently that is supposed to pick out photos and videos that are nearly identical so you can easily delete duplicates. Except it doesn’t actually recognize anything. It was suggesting “duplicates” that were of entirely different content, taken on different dates, that weren’t even remotely related to each other. Anyone who isn’t paying close attention and just hit delete on any of the suggested items, trusting that the algorithm works is going to be very sad when their photos and videos are gone. But hey, you’ll have more room on your phone and for the low low price of $60 PER MONTH WTF? They try to trick the low-attention-span population with their $14.99 per week price scam. 

Essentially, It actually took me MORE time to sift through each section to make sure the “smart” program wasn’t trying to delete stuff I wanted to keep. May as well just do it myself anyway.

reviews.title: “Old people”?
reviews.text:
You mean the people who literally invented the tech you used to develop your app? The tech you used to alienate their generation in your thoughtless, and oh SO typical little ad? I’m surprised you didn’t just say “boomers”. Seriously, what is the matter with you? Old people. Seriously?? 

I hail from GenX so I was raised by Baby Boomers. My generation had record stores, book stores, MTV when it actually was MTV. We experienced the world rather than a computer generated imitation of A world. We tuned into 89X before it was 89X and was a show on 88.7 that played  music that could not be heard anywhere else except that station after 7:00 or college radio when we could get a full signal. Bands like Joy Division, Pixies, Skinny Puppy, Ministry, Jane’s, Primus, Bauhaus… NONE of which would’ve or could have existed without the generation before us who also INVENTED ROCK & ROLL. None of that auto-tuned trash you listen to today would exist without those “old people”.

You know, really it’s just about respect. You didn’t need to put ANYONE on blast like that. Old, young, male, female. There’s no reason to ostracize anyone at all. Doing so isn’t exactly smart. I mean how many “old” people do you think would download your app after you call them out like they’re addle-brained and helpless? Genius.

reviews.text:
I purchased the Cleanup app but unfortunately, I haven’t been able to use it at all. Every time I open the app and start the cleaning process, it immediately crashes and closes.

I suspect this might be because my file library is large, but the app should ideally be able to process files in segments instead of shutting down completely. At the moment, the app is unusable for me, which makes the purchase feel wasted. I hope the developers can address this issue in a future update.

reviews.title: The 4.7 Rate is Deceiving
reviews.text:
Am I the only one who is tired of seeing ads targeting “old people” who don’t know how to use technology? It’s 2026. Give it a rest! 
Many recent reviews have stated that after the initial trial period, the creator is going to charge $8 a week. WHAT???!!! Besides, If it’s truly an app that helps eliminate duplicate photos, why would I need to pay a small ransom to continue to use it? The duplicates should be eliminated during the first week or so of use; certainly within a month. Why not just be honest up front? Any reasonable person understands that nothing is truly free. I have no problem paying them for their work and maintenance of the app but $8 is excessive by any standards for what we’re paying them to do. They must be hoping that we’ll install it and forget about it. I haven’t seen anyone respond to any of the users’ comments or complaints about this app which is a red flag that tells me that they are not monitoring customers concerns and there’s no access to the creators once you install it. I’ll continue to look for alternatives and meanwhile go through the daunting task of doing it myself.

reviews.title: Great app if would work properly
reviews.text: Unfortunately, this app doesn’t work properly. It takes a very long time to load and delete items, and the “similar photos” feature is very inaccurate — it often marks completely different pictures as duplicates just because they have the same background. Because of how slow it is, you end up risking deleting large parts of your gallery, when doing it manually one by one would actually be faster and safer. Overall, it’s very disappointing, especially after paying for the subscription. I feel like I’ve wasted my money.
